svg.aria-label: A3-01 — the error budget re-ranks itself when you change the assumed gauge accuracy
svg.desc: Horizontal dot plot of six error sources against their relative effect on the fitted gas in place, in percent, with three markers per row for the three assumed pressure standard deviations of 22.5, 45 and 90 psia. Only the random pressure scatter moves with the assumption: it runs 0.6621, 1.3242, 2.6483 percent across the three assumptions, while the shared calibration bias of 25 psia stays at 0.8624 percent, psig supplied as psia at 0.5037 percent, the deviation-factor correlation choice at 0.3326 percent, the standard-basis difference at 0.2312 percent, and a uniform multiplicative Z error of 5 percent at effectively zero, 3.1e-14 percent, because a uniform rescaling of the ordinate leaves the x-intercept alone. At the smallest assumed sigma the shared calibration bias ranks first and the random scatter second; at the other two the order reverses. The accompanying table gives the rank of every source under each assumption.
